links.outcome: Radiologist missed iPE rate with AI in clinical workflow versus before AI
links.effect: Missed iPEs by radiologists fell from 50% (cohort 1) to 7.1% after AI implementation, P < 0.001; standalone AI sensitivity 90-95%, PPV 69-95%.
links.quote: The rate of missed iPEs by radiologists dropped to 7.1% after AI implementation, showing a significant improvement ( P < 0.001).

links.outcome: 90-day mortality before versus after AI implementation
links.effect: No significant decrease in 90-day mortality despite improved detection; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).
links.quote: The survival analysis showed no significantly decreased 90-day mortality rate, with a hazards ratio of 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).

links.outcome: Missed incidental pulmonary embolisms and 90-day mortality after AI implementation
links.effect: Missed iPEs decreased from 50% to 7.1% (P < 0.001), but 90-day mortality did not significantly decrease: hazards ratio 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).
links.quote: The survival analysis showed no significantly decreased 90-day mortality rate, with a hazards ratio of 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).

links.outcome: AI sensitivity for incidental pulmonary embolism
links.effect: AI sensitivity was 95% in cohort 1 and 90% in cohort 2, indicating that some confirmed iPEs were not detected by AI.
links.quote: In cohort 2 (mean age 69 years, 47% female [n = 1567], 53% male [n = 1767]), the prevalence of confirmed iPEs was 1.7% (56/3334), with AI detecting 59 suspicious cases (sensitivity 90%, specificity 99%, PPV 95%, NPV 99%).

links.effect: The 90-day mortality rate did not significantly decrease with a hazards ratio of 0.95.
links.quote: The survival analysis showed no significantly decreased 90-day mortality rate, with a hazards ratio of 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).
